segment:
The head came upright and the lips drew back in a smile that didn’t reach the eyes, and he sat forward with an audible creak from the couch.
She took a slow breath and stepped into the room. He said nothing; the smile dropped away into a plain, curious expression. His arms lay on the arms of the couch as if to hold him still in place. His face was young, without the sharp lines she associated with the other people here—a few years older than she was, perhaps, though the hair might be dyed. He might be a researcher; his face had that alert, slightly abstracted quality of someone who understood the work being done and wasn’t afraid to do it. He was an excellent-looking specimen, well put-together and not self-conscious about it. She would probably have found him interesting enough for a conversation at a party, if she’d met him elsewhere.
text:
When Mara walked into the common room at six fifteen, someone was already there. Someone younger, it seemed.
She couldn’t make out the face behind the blond hair. But the body was fine enough, leaning back on the couch with bare legs crossed and arms flung in opposite directions, one palm pressing the padded wall and the other wrist resting on the low table beside him.
She stood stock-still by the doorway for a moment, aware of her breath and of his awareness that she was here. He stirred and tilted his head; a face turned toward her, expressionless.

segment:
It would have been the sort of person she would ordinarily have ignored; one more unconsidered body among many. But now, in this place and at this time, he was the only other human presence she knew. She let out an unconscious sigh and stepped forward toward the couch, stopping to slide her backpack from her shoulders and set it beside the door.
The person sat up with a rustle of cotton fabric. As he moved, Mara saw that he wore what looked like pajamas. The black shirt was unbuttoned to show the upper part of a pale chest, and the right arm was bare above the elbow, where he had rolled his sleeve. The other arm stayed covered.
“Good evening,” she said. She could hear her own voice in the quiet room; it sounded very young. “I’m Mara Vale.”
The person looked blank. Then he made a small, abrupt movement; his eyes met hers with what looked like recognition, and he smiled.
“Good evening,” he said. “You’re new, right? I’m Jonah Reed.” He got up from the couch, a bit too tall to make it comfortable to sit with crossed legs, and held out his hand. “Adrian told us to expect you.”

segment:
The room was large, open, and quiet except for the white noise of the fountain in the corner. The broad windows opposite were high enough to obscure the view from outside, but she had no illusion that he wouldn’t be able to hear every sound she made, from footsteps on the polished wood floor to the way her breath moved her chest beneath the dress.
He didn’t speak or move again; he just lay there, still and apparently relaxed, watching her. She didn’t feel obliged to introduce herself.
Adrian was still at the meeting room off the common room; Mara had been able to see the sign on the door as she came in, and the lights were still on behind the frosted glass.
She looked at the blond man. He looked back at her, head still resting on his hand, other arm loosely supporting himself, legs crossed.
And then he smiled, just a little, lips not even really curling, and sat up straight.
